As mentioned, it's scenes like that that make me trust my safety gear. I haven't seen the full accident footage, but he managed to do that with his car and walked away.

In my M6 GT3, I'm effectively a part of the car. When I wear my harness properly, I can turn my head from side to side, move it forward an inch or two, move my arms enough to reach the controls - which have to be close to me, and move the lower parts of my legs. The upper parts move, but not far and not without forcing them. In the event of an accident, there's almost nothing of me that will move or have anything to move into.

If I know I'm going to crash, I'll tuck my head down as far forward as I can - pre-tensing the HANS and cross my arms across my chest. I can get into that position into a fraction of a second. From there, if the car is full of smoke or fire, I know to follow my harness down to find the central lock of my harness. One push on that and I'm free - it just breaks away and I'm able to slide out of the by holding the door as it opens and pulling myself out with it. You probably don't notice, but my GT3 car even has an escape hatch on the roof, just in case.

So, yeah... I trust my safety gear absolutely. I've often said that I'd have not raced in the older cars. I'm a big fan of statistics and old-school racing wasn't safe enough for me to consider doing it.
